blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Possible from direct local governance-mutable controls, not merely Upstream. Official documentation lists chain-isolated, non-fungible Ethereum and Fraxtal sdUSD receipts representing dUSD supplied into dLEND. No usable supply shares are available, so both deployments were measured directly: at Ethereum block 26224761 (2026-10-19T06:14:23Z), totalSupply()=480792299440018849696901 and convertToAssets(totalSupply())=492480.64327662665 dUSD; at Fraxtal block 42789902 (2026-10-19T06:15:15Z), totalSupply()=37179813323 and convertToAssets(totalSupply())=42805.735228 dUSD. On the common underlying dUSD-claim denomination, total 535286.3785046267 dUSD implies Ethereum approximately 92.0032% and Fraxtal 7.9968%; Ethereum is material. Ethereum token 0x7cb20517776636ed76b68edb3d99dcce356abf02 has DStakeTokenV2 implementation 0x9c278036c3c4529472751502dfc71bb1f0a3bfd4 and ProxyAdmin 0xbe90db309b80357631069b689fc3481aca2c65be owned by TimelockController 0x18cb0eb73d953ed20f2157ce6bde2a85e30e681b; its getMinDelay()=86400. The same timelock has DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the token and may call migrateCore() to install a candidate router. DStakeTokenV2 has no share-transfer pause/blacklist, and burnFromRouter requires allowance unless its supplied initiator equals owner. The current router 0x6d4a26fe926e88fee41a9fddeda3b50bf98f1ddb is verified DStakeRouterV2Incident, whose inherited solver withdrawal paths pass msg.sender as initiator, so there is no presently active arbitrary-holder seizure path. Nevertheless proxy upgrades and admin router replacement are direct Possible; a 24-hour delay does not make them upstream-only. The current router also has active PAUSER_ROLE at the same timelock, paused()=false, and can globally stop existing-holder redemptions while share transfers continue. Fraxtal's below-threshold token still uses implementation 0x0f51b15939a42bd995ecd3a2c151dc58621856c6 and ProxyAdmin 0xde914ec384346fea47339e5086d2d399b7f4733b owned by 0x0bafada2a5824864720873ee40cd960b36445212; that peripheral upgrade control is disclosed. Pinned asset() confirms the dUSD parent on each chain. Parent dUSD is independently Possible under the same decision procedure, but local direct Possible takes precedence regardless of inherited exposure. The terms' general interface restrictions do not establish a live token blacklist.

oracleRisk.summary: sdUSD is an ERC-4626 receipt whose conversion value is vault accounting over dUSD supplied to dLEND, and dUSD's own price is hard-coded at $1 inside dLEND, so no external feed prices sdUSD or dUSD directly. dLEND borrower collateral is valued through the issuer-published feed set: the dTRINITY USD Oracle Aggregator (Ethereum 0xC40f4303505320F782972ad4756eD2A7390a9d9C, Fraxtal 0xFA7560956807d95DCeF22990DdD92e38DbAf5cDd) over Chainlink market feeds on Ethereum, Api3 market and fundamental feeds on Fraxtal, and issuer fundamental feeds for yield-bearing collateral. Collateral mispricing or liquidation bad debt transmits to sdUSD NAV. The inventory is exact and dated, but feed heartbeats, deviation thresholds, fallback ordering and a single-feed failure bound are not published.

branchApplicability.rationale: sdUSD is excluded as dLEND collateral and holds no borrower positions or liquidation engine of its own; its only pricing path is ERC-4626 share accounting over dLEND-supplied dUSD. The dLEND collateral feeds are the parent dUSD's valuation authority and are already reviewed under dUSD's oracle profile, so they are recorded here as the inherited top-level feed set instead of being declared sdUSD-specific borrower branches.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: sdUSD is a chain-isolated dSTAKE ERC-4626 receipt on Ethereum and Fraxtal. Official dTRINITY documentation states that these deployments are non-fungible across chains and cannot be natively bridged. Users can swap into intermediary assets before bridging and swap back on the destination chain; that is not an sdUSD bridge mint path.
